To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the integration of GIS and statistics analysis in a client/server architecture is feasible, that the R statistical software is well suited to be the core of the server side, that the use of the GDAL library and its OGR interface is the best choice to manage the geographical data, and that a Web interface is the most convenient way for the user to access to the server side.
the use of R as the central component of the architecture is a good choice.

R can be successfully used for GIS applications, that the R language can be extended by the addition of new data types, and that the R language has a very good support for object-oriented programming.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a client/server system based on R and a GIS system that will be used for data analysis, data mining and spatial analysis of large datasets.
the development and implementation of a R centric client server system that will provide a platform for the development of multi purpose geographical analysis tools.
the development of a R centric platform for multi purpose geographical analyses on heterogeneous multi source geographical data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

R is the best choice for the implementation of the GIS and the statistical analysis of heterogeneous multi source data, with the following constraints: a) the data must be stored in a relational database; b) the data must have an associated metadata; and, c) the data must follow a standard format (such as the XML).
the R language is a powerful tool for the statistical analysis of spatially distributed data, and that it has the potential to be a useful tool in the analysis of geographical information systems.
the R statistical system has the potential to become a powerful platform for geographical analysis on heterogeneous data sources, but it requires some additional developments and improvements.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the R language is an excellent tool for the analysis and visualization of spatial data.
R can be considered a good choice for the analysis of geographical data, and the integration between R and GIS is an important step for the analysis of spatial data.
we have developed an efficient architecture to perform multi purpose geographical analysis with a client/server architecture and a R centric approach to deal with the complexity of the system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
R provides an elegant platform with a rich set of functions for statistical data analysis and mathematical computations.
R can be used in a client server architecture with the possibility of sharing heterogeneous data and to perform complex analysis.
it is possible to build an R based system that provides a powerful environment for statistical analysis and geographical information processing on multi source data.
